summary: The Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is an interactive, bilingual (English and Arabic) aerospace engineering simulation using real telemetry data from NASA and ESA. Players manage a crew of 4 on a 30 Sol mission on the Lunar South Pole (Shackleton Rim) or Mars (Jezero Crater Delta). They have to manage a systems integration of life support, power and radiation. The game provides a solution to the problem of survival in deep space habitats by taking complicated differential equations such as NASA BVAD metabolic rates, ISS 98% water recycling, Kilopower KRUSTY nuclear energy and NASA-STD-3001 radiation limits and simplifying them so players can make decisions. Players have to manage power, survive sandstorms or 50 hour long lunar eclipses and deal with tactical emergencies while also keeping within the tight mass limits of their lander payload. This is important as it connects STEM theory to real aerospace systems engineering and inspires students to learn about the critical engineering trade-offs that are needed to keep humans alive beyond earth.
details: The Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is an interactive dual language (English/Arabic) aerospace engineering simulation game where the player must manage an integrated O₂/CO2 system (ppCO₂), a water recovery system, calorie intake, battery storage and total ionising radiation exposure. The game will simulate a 30 Sol surface mission taking place either at the Lunar South Pole (Shackleton Rim) or Mars (Jezero Crater Delta). The game will teach students the connection between theory-based STEM subjects and aerospace systems engineering by allowing them to experience the real world through a game. They will understand how humans can survive off-world due to the integrated nature of mass and energy balances within the system. Our aim is to inspire students and space enthusiasts by encouraging them to think critically and solve problems related to systems engineering. We have created this project using HTML5, CSS3 (Tailwind CSS) and JavaScript (ES6+). We have implemented a range of tools to improve the game including Tone.js for creating sci-fi procedural audio effects, Font Awesome for aerospace telemetry icons and Google Fonts (Inter, Orbitron and Cairo for full Arabic (RTL) support). The unique aspect of this project is that it uses real data from NASA and ESA papers to create a real time differential equation and SVG. This includes metabolic rates from NASA BVAD, the 98% water recovery rate from the ISS, kilopower KRUSTY nuclear reaction and NASA-STD-3001 radiation. We focused on making the game as accurate as possible, being dual language, having realistic trade-offs such as automatic load shedding during brownouts and focusing on keeping the lander under mass.
